string.text: New anomalies have opened routes to uncharted parts of the Zone, including Grimwood. \n Scientists are intrigued by its unusual ecosystem: predators let weaker mutants pass deeper into the forest, then gather to feed. The forest itself may be a psi anomaly that affects living minds. Entering is a huge risk for any stalker, but Grimwood can shorten the journey north and may hold unknown artifacts.

This is the Zone’s current northern border. Many ruined buildings shelter the numerous mutants here. They emerge to catch careless stalkers who dare to venture this far. From time to time, zombified stalkers come out of the dark fog north of Jupiter, as if continuing their journey through the Zone. There are also rumors of a new nest of “psi-bloodsuckers”.

After the Super-Emission, Clear Sky abandoned its base, and these swamps became true marshes of death.
No one clears out the mutants anymore, so lower-tier creatures such as dogs and fleshes are everywhere.
These mutants hide when a wave of zombies or izlom reaches the swamps.
Predators sometimes wander here too, so stay alert. It is unclear what Clear Sky is doing here; perhaps they are settling scores with the renegades sheltering in the area.
Rumor has it that an old swamp bloodsucker lives here.

The Vehicle Graveyard was once considered a southern location, but is now part of the Middle Zone. 
 Empty vehicle hulks lie piled like corpses; metal eaten away by anomalies groans in a strange, breathing chorus. 
 Duty and Freedom compete for stashes and artifacts, while mutants push south toward the Dark Valley and Cordon. 
 For unknown reasons, a pseudogiant sometimes seems to guard their migration. Experienced Renegade groups have settled nearby, likely searching for Duty weapon stashes.

The Cordon has become an inhospitable place. \n Its former calm is gone: lower-tier mutants stream in from the north without pause, so numerous that the military abandoned its position at the Southern Checkpoint. Clear Sky is studying this phenomenon, hoping it will reveal the origin of the Gloom anomaly. Rumors about Sidorovich’s stashes, after he hurriedly left his bunker, also draw bandits here. They keep their distance, though—the mutants are too numerous.

The Garbage is no longer the quiet haven between the Zone’s south and north. Duty had to abandon its northern checkpoint, and only a dead campfire remains of the Flea Market’s old gatherings. The remaining bandits prey on stalkers, while Duty sends scouts to assess a possible return. New anomalies attract scientists and may draw mercenaries too. Rumor says a psydog hides in the forest and occasionally comes out to hunt.

After the military left this area, underground mutants crawled out of their lairs. Military patrols still pass through sometimes, perhaps scouting to keep others from occupying their base. Various toughs also wander here, usually after leftover supplies at the base or underground, or searching for a stash belonging to Duty.

After the super-emission at Lab X-16, strange things began. \n Poisonous air and powerful anomalies drove Sultan’s bandits and even the military out of the Valley. Zombies and snorks keep emerging from underground. Now this is almost the Zone’s north, where every day is a fight to survive. Bandits return for old stashes, stalkers seek artifacts, and the military may be trying to stop the mutants and learn where they came from.

Army Warehouses. \n The events later called the “Exodus of Freedom” took place here. The army base is abandoned, and the Barrier has long been deserted; only the landscape and ruined fortifications recall the past. Scouts from Duty and Freedom can be found here. Freedom may be evacuating its many army stashes, while Duty watches closely. Sometimes “fresh” zombie stalkers stand motionless here, perhaps returning by habit to places from their former lives.

A dangerous northern region. \n It once had at least some people, but now it is almost deserted. The eastern forest is a breeding ground for predators that spread through the Zone. Changes in the anomaly fields give them cover, and neither cleanup squads nor the military reach this place. The idea of burning it with artillery was rejected after scientists objected. Only a fool enters the Red Forest at night or without proper gear.

The settlement used to be surrounded by a dense radioactive shroud, but to everyone’s surprise, radiation has now subsided.\nBandits and renegades forced out of Dark Valley often take shelter among the settlement’s ruins.\nSome wounded or lesser mutants may hide here too, which can attract predators looking for vulnerable prey.

It is relatively easy to enter Pripyat, but much harder to leave alive. The Monolith faction has settled here, and how they survive remains a mystery. Rumor says they possess an artifact that hides their shelter from mutants. The city is also full of the Gloom, mutants, and anomalies.

A dangerous place that has not been fully explored. \n Humanoid mutants such as snorks and even burers are often seen here, though no one knows where they come from. Some say underground tunnels connect to the Dark Valley; others believe the catacombs are linked to Lab X-16. Weaker mutants avoid the area, while its unknown anomalies attract Clear Sky, stalkers, and mercenaries.

As you head north, the air grows stale and harder to breathe. \n The ground becomes sticky with mud, and the black fog appears. Any sensible stalker turns back: few return from the Gloom intact. Little is known about this anomaly. What is certain is that sleeping inside it leads to madness. The Gloom is also teeming with mutants, including so-called “alpha hybrids”.
